decisions.rationale: Full name of a single defined syndrome (van der Woude syndrome) with no further categorization, so it is a specific disease mention.
Cleft palate is a single defined congenital disease named as a noun phrase in 'susceptibility locus for cleft palate', not modifying another concept.
Repeated full mention of van der Woude syndrome in the abstract; duplicate mentions are annotated separately.
Abbreviation VWS defined as van der Woude syndrome in 'van der Woude syndrome ( VWS )' is annotated as its own separate synonymous mention.
Slash-joined coordination 'cleft lip / palate' denotes two separate diseases (cleft lip and cleft palate) within one contiguous string.
Abbreviation CL / P is the defined short form of the composite 'cleft lip / palate' and refers to the same two separate diseases, so it stays composite.
Standalone reference to the specific disease cleft palate in the list of VWS features; it is not a modifier.
Abbreviation CP defined as cleft palate in 'cleft palate ( CP )' is a separate synonymous mention of a specific disease.
Bifid uvula is a named specific congenital malformation listed as a clinical sign; it is a concrete condition rather than a general term.
Hypodontia is a named specific dental anomaly (congenital tooth agenesis) listed as a clinical feature of VWS.
Abbreviation H defined as hypodontia in 'hypodontia ( H )' is annotated as a separate synonymous mention of the specific disease.
VWS used as the name of the syndrome in 'The expression of VWS' refers to the single specific disease.
Abbreviation CL / P in 'occurrence of CL / P and CP' refers to two separate diseases (cleft lip and cleft palate), so it is a composite mention.
Abbreviation CP used as a disease noun in 'occurrence of CL / P and CP' refers to the single specific disease cleft palate.
Abbreviation CP used as a disease noun in 'recurrence risk for CP' refers to the single specific disease cleft palate.
VWS used as a noun referring to the disease in 'descendants with VWS' is the abbreviation of van der Woude syndrome.
'clefts' refers to a family of multiple cleft defects (cleft lip and/or palate types) rather than one specific disease, so it is a class; it is not as general as excluded terms.
The generic term 'syndrome' is explicitly excluded as a general term and does not name a specific disease.
VWS used as a noun in 'kindred with VWS' refers to the disease itself, not as a modifier of another noun.
Abbreviation CP used as a disease noun in 'individuals with CP' refers to the single specific disease cleft palate.
VWS used as a noun in 'clinical signs of VWS' refers to the syndrome itself, not as a modifier.
VWS in 'the VWS gene at 1p32-41' modifies the noun 'gene' to name a locus, so it is used as a modifier of another concept.
Abbreviation CP used as a noun in 'probability of CP in an individual' refers to the specific disease cleft palate and does not modify another noun phrase.
VWS in 'other VWS pedigrees' modifies the noun 'pedigrees', so it functions as a modifier of another concept.
